# Introduction 

**Dunning** - The word stems from the 17th-century verb dun, meaning to demand payment of a debt

Dunning identifies specific debt as outstanding or that is to be reclaimed due to payment refusal.

Dunning provides a toolset, aimed to expedite the recovery of the outstanding debt, the tools include various types of customer interactions or activities that entail service suppression.

Dunning is responsible to determine when outstanding debt needs to be tracked and managed and when the recovery process for that outstanding debt is done.

## Dunning - Business Pillars

- **Dunning strategy** collectively defines the applicable dunning treatment, it defines the appropriate toolset of actions using which the system will attempt to reclaim the outstanding debt.
- **Dunning rule** defines when a given dunning instruction should be used for facilitating the dunning treatment.
- **Dunning case** represent the end-to-end life cycle of a specific dunning treatment from identification to closure.

Following table captures an example of a Dunning business illustrating various business events and dunning rules excuted and actions taken during a timeline captured in first column.

# Use Cases 

## Administration of Dunning Strategy and Dunning Rules:

The Dunning Case API can be called by the dunning department of a company via e.g. an administrative tool, to create update or delete the dunning Strategy and the dunning rules, based on the dunning strategy of the company. Some examples:

- A new rule is created to trigger one more notification to the customer, e.g. after 10 days, via email, while the existing one is an SMS sent in 7 days
- A new rule is created, which is triggered when the customer opens a new trouble ticket
- An existing rule is updated, with a more aggressive action (e.g., call from an agent instead of SMS notification)
- A new Strategy is created, to cover the dunning process of a new customer segmentation (e.g. mid value customers, while the existing one cover the segments mass and high value)
- A Strategy is updated with extra rules
- A Strategy is updated as obsolete, due to special period (e.g. Covid-19 makes obsolete the “hard” strategy)
- The dunning strategy applicable to a specific customer account is updated in the system by an administrator for special reasons. This could be done by deploying specific Dunning Strategy with more relaxed rules and actions, and with conditions that match certain specific customers or types or customers.

Example:

![](data:image/png;base64,)

**Figure 3. Administration of Dunning Strategy and Dunning Rules** Main actors:

- A Dunning administrator
- A dunning administrative user interface, with journeys of managing dunning rules and Strategy, using the Dunning Case API
- A platform capable of storing the Dunning Strategy and rules reference data Use case steps:

1. The Dunning administrator creates a new dunning Strategy in line with business requirements, e.g. a Strategy to apply in high value customers;

![](data:image/png;base64,)

![](data:image/png;base64,)

2. The Dunning administrator creates one or more Dunning rules applicable to dunning strategy and apply them on the dunning Strategy, e.g. that customers of specific tariff plans and with debt above a specific amount are handled by the dunning Strategy; Part of the dunning rule creation are the following:
3. The Dunning administrator specifies the set of conditions applicable to each Dunning Rule, e.g. minimum debt = 50 euros and minimum time period passed 7 days;
4. The Dunning administrator specifies the type of dunning action that will take place, when the conditions of the dunning rules are met, e.g. send an SMS reminder or apply a penalty charge.

Dunning Strategy and rules are commonly created and configured in the Dunning Platform through the user interface or reference data, and not though external interfaces. Consequently, this operation would not be mandatory in the API.

## Getting the list of Dunning Cases of a Customer:

Whenever a customer enters the dunning process, a dunning case is linked to their customer account debt and it contains all details pertaining to the debt, such as dunning case rules and interactions. Typically, these are the steps that are followed to get a dunning case’s details for a customer.

1. A customer’s outbound mobile calls have been barred on the network due to a lack of payment on their account despite several written warnings.
2. The customer calls the care team to complain and understand why his service has been curtailed.
3. The care agent logs into the Customer Information system.
4. The agent runs a query to fetch Dunning case details for a customer account number. This step will call the DunningCase GET operation.
5. The Debt and Collection Management system returns any active Dunning case details.
6. Depending on the information received in the response, the agent acts as per the dunning rules specified for the customer (Consumer or Enterprise).

A customer might have also be notified of the Dunning Case via postal mail or other notification media with the id or the URL to view the detail. The customer then:

1. Would open the URL of the notification or would log into his self-care portal app or web site.
2. Fetch his dunning case by id or run a query against this customer account number.
3. The Debt and Collection Management system returns any active Dunning case details.
4. Customer sees the detail of the Dunning Case and the options available for him to cancel the debt.

Example:

![](data:image/png;base64,)

![](data:image/png;base64,)

![](data:image/jpeg;base64,)

**Figure 4. Getting the list of Dunning Cases of a Customer**

Main actors:

- The customer
- The Self Care portal with journeys to show customer if he has any Dunning Case open.
- The CRM application, with a screen to query Dunning Cases of a customer.
- platform capable of storing the Dunning Cases.

## Creating a Dunning Case on a Customer Billing Account:

Normally the Debt and Collection Management system is the system responsible for evaluation the Dunning Strategy and Creating the Dunning Cases:

1. Policy Events are triggered
2. System checks if Policy Conditions are met.
3. Corresponding Policy Actions are automated.

Each of the actions imply the automatic creation of a Dunning Case, in accordance to the Dunning Strategy.

The Collection Management system may however expose an administrative API to create Dunning Cases that are generated from other sources or applications, like for instance when a company has different IT stacks and need to communicate Dunning Cases from one stack to the other, or when there are different Debt and Collection Management systems, and one must communicate the Dunning Cases to the other.

# Support of polymorphism and extension patterns

Support of polymorphic collections and types and schema based extension is provided by means of a list of generic meta-attributes that we describe below. Polymorphism in collections occurs when entities inherit from base entities, for instance DunningActionNotification and DunningActionProductOrder inheriting properties from the abstract DunningActionEntity.

Generic support of polymorphism and pattern extensions is described in the TMF API Guidelines.

The @type attribute provides a way to represent the actual class type of an entity. For example, A DunningActionEntity instance might be an instances of DunningActionNotification or DunningActionProductOrder or DunningActionCustomerBill. The @type gives this information. All resources and sub-resources of this API have a @type attributes that can be provided when this is useful.

The @schemaLocation property can be used in resources to allow specifying user-defined properties of an Entity or to specify the expected characteristics of an entity.

The @baseType attribute gives a way to provide explicitly the base class of a given resource that has been extended.

| dunningCondition | A PolicyCondition. A PolicyCondition clause is a collection ofindividual policy conditions, treated as a single unit that iscombined with a PolicyRule. ### DunningStrategy resource

Describes company strategy to be applied for different dunning situations. It must be easily configurable to describe the dunning rules to apply to a case, the order in which to apply them, the events that trigger dunning rules evaluation and the actions that must be taken.

### DunningCase resource

The DunningCase represents full dunning lifecyle. When a customer enters the dunning process, a dunning case is linked to their customer account debt and it contains all details pertaining to the debt, such as applied dunning rules, interactions. The status of a dunning case evolves according to internal or external events (payments made by the customer, payment schedule granted, etc.).

### 10 notifications are defined for this API.

![](data:image/png;base64,)

![](data:image/png;base64,)

Notifications related to DunningRule:

- Create Event
- Delete Event
- Attribute Value Change Event Notifications related to DunningStrategy:
- Create Event
- Delete Event
- Attribute Value Change Event Notifications related to DunningCase:
- Create Event
- Delete Event
- Attribute Value Change Event
- Status Change Event The notification structure for all notifications in this API follow the pattern depicted by the figure below. A notification event resource (depicted by "SpecificEvent" placeholder) is a sub class of a generic Event structure containing at least an id of the event occurrence (eventId), an event timestamp (eventTime), and the name of the resource (eventType). This notification structure owns an event payload structure ("SpecificEventPayload" placeholder) linked to the resource concerned by the notification using the resource name as access field ("resourceName" placeholder).

# API OPERATIONS 

Every operation consists of two parts:

- REQUEST: Publish a message on a 'commandRequest' channel.
- RESPONSE: Subscribe to the corresponding 'commandReply' channel to receive the response.

Remember the following Async Uniform Contract:

| Operation on Entities | Uniform Async API Operation | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Query One Entity | retrieveResource | retrieve must be used to retrievea representation of a resource. |
| Query Entities | listResource | list must be used to retrieve alist of resources. |
| Create Entity | createResource | create must be used to create anew resource |
| Partial Update of an Entity | patchResource | patch must be used to partiallyupdate a resource |
| Remove an Entity | deleteResource | delete must be used to removea resource |

Filtering and attribute selection rules are described in the TMF Async Design Guidelines.

Notifications are also described in a subsequent section.

### Updates partially a DunningRule

```
PATCH /dunningRule/{id}?fields=…
```

**Description**

This operation allows partial updates of a DunningRule entity. Support of json/merge ([https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7396)](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7396) is mandatory, support of json/patch ([http://tools.ietf.org/](http://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc5789) [html/rfc5789)](http://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc5789) is optional. Note: If the update operation yields to the creation of sub-resources or relationships, the same rules concerning mandatory sub-resource attributes and default value settings in the POST operation applies to the PATCH operation. Hence these tables are not repeated here.

| href |  |
| id |  |
| @baseType | @baseType is immutable |
| @schemaLocation | @schemaLocation is immutable |
| @type | @type is immutable |

| **Patchable Attributes** | **Rule** |
| --- | --- |
| dunningAction |  |
| dunningCondition |  |
| dunningEvent |  |
| name |  |

# NOTIFICATIONS 

Topic for DunningCase entity: {prefix}.dunning.v5.dunningCase.notificationEvent

Topic for DunningRule entity: {prefix}.dunning.v5.dunningRule.notificationEvent

Topic for DunningStrategy entity: {prefix}.dunning.v5.dunningStrategy.notificationEvent

For every single of operation on the entities use the following templates and provide sample notification message payloads.

It is assumed that consumers will subscribe to the notificationEvent channel to receive notifications, and that the server component will post notifications to that channel.

## Publish Event to listener

Here’s an example of a notification received by the consumer. In this example “EVENT TYPE” should be replaced by one of the notification types supported by this API (see Notification resources Models section) and EVENT BODY refers to the data structure of the given notification type.

{ "event": { EVENT BODY }, "eventType": "EVENT\_TYPE" }

For detailed examples on the general TM Forum notification mechanism, see the TMF Async Design Guidelines.
